questions.prompt: Which direction should the cost calculation follow?

choices.label: Backward from the last stairs toward the starting stairs.
choices.feedback: Working backward makes both possible future finishing costs available before solving the current stair.

choices.label: Forward, always choosing the cheaper immediate next stair.
choices.feedback: Working backward makes both possible future finishing costs available before solving the current stair.

choices.label: From the cheapest stair anywhere in the array.
choices.feedback: Working backward makes both possible future finishing costs available before solving the current stair.

questions.prompt: How should the finishing cost at a stair be computed?

choices.label: Only the smaller immediate price of the next two stairs.
choices.feedback: Each choice must include the entire remaining route, and only one of those routes is taken.

choices.label: Its cost plus both future finishing costs.
choices.feedback: Each choice must include the entire remaining route, and only one of those routes is taken.

choices.label: Its cost plus the smaller finishing cost of the next one or two stairs.
choices.feedback: Each choice must include the entire remaining route, and only one of those routes is taken.

questions.prompt: Which values should “i” visit, and in what order?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: Start “i” at the length of “cost” minus 3, change it by “-1” each time, and stop before “-1”.

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range((len(cost) // 3), -1, -1):” instead of “for i in range(len(cost) - 3, -1, -1):”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list index out of range; the expected result is 15.

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range((len(cost) + 3), -1, -1):” instead of “for i in range(len(cost) - 3, -1, -1):”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list index out of range; the expected result is 15.

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This uses “for i in range((len(cost) * 3), -1, -1):” instead of “for i in range(len(cost) - 3, -1, -1):”. On this test, it raises IndexError: list index out of range; the expected result is 15.

questions.prompt: What should “cost[i]” store after this step?

choices.label: Option A
choices.feedback: This uses “cost[i] += min(cost[(i - 1)], cost[i + 2])” instead of “cost[i] += min(cost[i + 1], cost[i + 2])”. On this test, it returns 2; the expected result is 6.

choices.label: Option B
choices.feedback: This uses “cost[i] += min(cost[(i * 1)], cost[i + 2])” instead of “cost[i] += min(cost[i + 1], cost[i + 2])”. On this test, it returns 2; the expected result is 6.

choices.label: Option C
choices.feedback: Add the minimum of “cost[i + 1]”, “cost[i + 2]” to “cost[i]”.

choices.label: Option D
choices.feedback: This uses “cost[i] += min(cost[(i // 1)], cost[i + 2])” instead of “cost[i] += min(cost[i + 1], cost[i + 2])”. On this test, it returns 2; the expected result is 6.
